articles.title: Empagliflozin and other SGLT2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure and preserved ejection fraction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.snippet: Hamid AK, Tayem AA, Al-Aish ST, Al Sakini AS, Hadi DD, Al-Aish RT | Therapeutic advances in cardiovascular disease | 2024 | Systematic Review; Journal Article; Meta-Analysis
articles.full_summary: A meta-analysis of 8 RCTs found that SGLT2 inhibitors decreased the risk of cardiovascular hospitalization in patients with HFpEF, but not cardiovascular death.
articles.key_finding: Our meta-analysis showed a decreased risk of cardiovascular hospitalization but not death due to cardiovascular causes or other causes.
articles.population: HFpEF patients

response.global_summary:
SGLT2 inhibitors, such as empagliflozin and dapagliflozin, have demonstrated significant benefits for patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) [2][3][4][5][7][10][12][13][17][18]. These benefits include improvements in patient-reported symptoms, physical limitations, and exercise function, as well as reductions in hospitalizations for heart failure and cardiovascular death [1][2][3][4][5][7][12][13][17][18].

Several meta-analyses and randomized controlled trials consistently show that SGLT2 inhibitors reduce the risk of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) in HFpEF patients [4][5][13][18]. One meta-analysis reported a **risk ratio of 0.75** (95% CI 0.63-0.89) for this composite outcome [4]. Another systematic review and meta-analysis found a **pooled hazard ratio of 0.80** (95% CI: 0.74, 0.86, p < 0.001) for cardiovascular disease (CVD)/HFH outcomes in patients with HF with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction [5]. A more recent systematic review and meta-analysis reported an **odds ratio of 0.71** (95% CI: 0.66-0.75, P < 0.00001) for the primary composite endpoint and **0.69** (95% CI 0.64-0.74; P < 0.00001) for HFH [18]. The DELIVER study, a randomized controlled trial, specifically confirmed a **27% reduction** in the composite outcome of HFH plus cardiovascular mortality and a **21% reduction** in HFH with dapagliflozin in patients with mildly reduced or preserved LVEF, regardless of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) status [7]. Similarly, the EMPEROR-Preserved trial showed that empagliflozin reduced the risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.69-0.9, P < .001) [17]. Empagliflozin also reduced the combined risk of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, or an emergency/urgent heart failure visit requiring intravenous treatment by a **hazard ratio of 0.77** (95% CI, 0.67–0.87; P<0.0001) in patients with class II through IV heart failure with an ejection fraction of >40% [12].

These benefits extend to various subgroups, including males and females, those aged <65 and ≥65, different races (Black and White), and patients with varying estimated glomerular filtration rates (eGFR <60 and ≥60) and New York Heart Association (NYHA) classes (II and ≥III) [13]. The effectiveness of SGLT2 inhibitors in reducing the risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death with dapagliflozin has been observed in patients with a left ventricular ejection fraction of more than 40% [2]. Furthermore, a nationwide cohort study (REFINE-HFpEF) found that starting SGLT2 inhibitors was associated with a significantly lower risk of hospital admission for heart failure and all-cause mortality compared to DPP4 inhibitors or sulfonylureas in HFpEF patients with type 2 diabetes and high event rates [6]. The benefits of dapagliflozin on the primary outcome were consistent regardless of polypharmacy status in symptomatic HF patients with LVEF >40% [19].

Beyond clinical outcomes, SGLT2 inhibitors also demonstrate physiological improvements. Long-term SGLT2 inhibitor therapy has been shown to improve myocardial strain and diastolic function in HFpEF patients, with significant improvement in global longitudinal strain (ΔGLS: **−2.49% ± 0.54%** vs. −0.44% ± 0.52%, P < 0.001) after **6 months of treatment** [8]. In diabetic HFpEF patients, dapagliflozin significantly reduced myocardial fibrosis (mean ΔECV: **-3.5%** [95% CI -4.2 to -2.8]) compared to placebo (-0.8% [95% CI -1.3 to -0.4]; p < 0.001) [9]. SGLT2 inhibitors are also considered efficacious and safe for treating HFpEF in patients with comorbid chronic kidney disease (CKD), both with and without T2DM [11].

However, one meta-analysis indicated a **mixed direction** of effect, showing a decreased risk of cardiovascular hospitalization but *not* death due to cardiovascular causes or other causes [0]. This contrasts with other meta-analyses and trials that reported reductions in cardiovascular death or the composite of cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization [2][4][5][7][12][13][17][18].

key_findings.text: SGLT2 inhibitors significantly reduce the risk of heart failure hospitalization in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and those with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction.
SGLT2 inhibitors improve patient-reported symptoms, physical limitations, and exercise function in patients with chronic HFpEF.
Dapagliflozin reduces the combined risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death in patients with heart failure and a left ventricular ejection fraction of more than 40%.

SGLT2 inhibitors are effective in reducing the composite outcome of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization across various subgroups, including different ages, sexes, races, eGFR levels, and NYHA classes.
Long-term SGLT2 inhibitor therapy improves myocardial strain and diastolic function in HFpEF patients.
Dapagliflozin significantly reduces myocardial fibrosis in patients with HFpEF and type 2 diabetes.
SGLT2 inhibitors are efficacious and safe for treating HFpEF in patients with comorbid chronic kidney disease, with or without type 2 diabetes mellitus.
The benefits of dapagliflozin on the primary outcome are consistent regardless of polypharmacy status in symptomatic HF patients with LVEF >40%.

evidence_gaps: The specific role of ejection fraction and patient heterogeneity in the efficacy of SGLT2 inhibitors in HFpEF patients requires further research [14].
The effects of sotagliflozin on left ventricular mass in non-diabetic HFpEF patients are being investigated, but results are not yet available [16].
The full range of effects of dapagliflozin on cardiac damage mechanisms in diabetic patients with HFpEF is under investigation [15].
